title: Who Needs the Bomb?
gist: Teaser of a Foreign Affairs response in which Edelman and Miller rebut Rose Gottemoeller's claim that nuclear deterrence is failing; only the opening is available in the text.

insights.claim: Eric Edelman and Franklin Miller argue that reports of the death of nuclear deterrence are greatly exaggerated and that obituaries for nuclear weapons misapprehend the role these arms have played since 1945.
insights.speaker: Eric S. Edelman
insights.so_what: Defense-policy voices still back the nuclear triad, so expect continued support for modernization spending.
insights.quote: Reports of the death of nuclear deterrence are greatly exaggerated.

insights.claim: Rose Gottemoeller's July/August 2026 essay holds that nuclear weapons increasingly lack value and purpose, that deterrence is not working because nuclear escalation risk did not prevent conventional and hybrid war, and that the U.S. triad can do little to deter certain salvos.
insights.speaker: Rose Gottemoeller (as characterized by Edelman and Miller)
insights.so_what: Sets out the skeptic case that the responses contest; a live debate over the future of strategic stability.
insights.locator: In The Strange Defeat of Nuclear Deterrence
